findings.title: signal_receipt is a PRE-EXISTING kind that silently changed classification, altering two lane gauges
findings.detail: lib/fleet/worker-status.cjs adds signal_receipt to INFORMATIONAL_KINDS. Unlike capped_pool_broadcast, signal_receipt is NOT new -- it shipped to main in QF-20260906-162. Because classifyCoordinationRow checks INFORMATIONAL_KINDS before the DRAIN_SETS union, every pre-existing signal_receipt row flips from classification actionable (basis drain_set) to informational (basis informational_registry). Two consumers were not updated and were not in the SD's enumerated intended-change set: (a) lib/coordination/lane-pending-gauge.cjs:61, where receipts move out of the actionable count into informational and stop contributing to oldestActionableAgeMs; (b) lib/coordination/lane-dead-letter-gauge.cjs:75, where expired-unread receipts move from expired_unread into structurally_artifact_prone, LOWERING the reported dead-letter rate for whichever lane they map to.
findings.assessment: Direction of change is defensible and arguably desirable, since a delivery receipt is not an open ask and should not inflate an actionable-pending gauge or a dead-letter rate, and it is explicitly documented in the FR-1 docblock. But it is a real, measurable, cross-module change to an EXISTING kind, so gauge readings will shift discontinuously at merge. Flagged, not failed.
findings.secondary: lane-dead-letter-gauge.cjs's inline rationale for the else-branch reads that no DRAIN_SET ever owns this kind, so read_at was structurally never going to be stamped. That premise is now FALSE for signal_receipt and capped_pool_broadcast, which sit in all four DRAIN_SETS. The number it produces is still the intended one, but the comment justifying it has gone stale and will mislead the next reader.
findings.recommended_followup: Non-blocking: correct the lane-dead-letter-gauge else-branch comment, and note the expected one-time gauge step-change in the SD retro so the shift is not later mis-triaged as a delivery-failure improvement.

findings.title: Every WORK_ASSIGNMENT body is now mutated, and existing dispatch tests likely cover it vacuously
findings.detail: stampConstraintsBlock runs inside insertCoordinationRow for all WORK_ASSIGNMENT rows and always appends a block, including a none-recorded placeholder when nothing is found, mutating BOTH row.body and row.payload.body in place, and adding one strategic_directives_v2 read per WORK_ASSIGNMENT insert. Under the existing dispatch suites' supabase mocks the SD lookup throws and is swallowed by the fail-soft catch, so those 409 passing files do not by themselves prove body compatibility for a live dispatch; the dedicated tests/unit/coordinator/stamp-constraints-block.test.js (183 lines) is what actually covers the stamper.
findings.assessment: Low risk. In-place row mutation is the established pattern of three sibling stampers (stampEffortRecommendation, stampModelRecommendation, stampPremiseMeasurement) at the same choke point. Repo-wide grep finds NO consumer that parses a WORK_ASSIGNMENT body for a CONSTRAINTS block or asserts exact body equality; the only other hits are unrelated prompt templates under scripts/archive/. Oversize renders fail soft via capBodySafe -- the stamp is dropped with a warning, never truncated, never thrown, and the un-stamped assignment still inserts.

verdict_rationale: CONDITIONAL_PASS, not PASS: zero test regressions, a clean and fully verified resolveHoldProvenance revert, exact-count assertions incremented rather than loosened, and all export signatures backward compatible. Withheld from PASS solely because REG-1 changes the classification of signal_receipt, a kind that already existed on main, which shifts two lane-gauge readings that the SD did not enumerate as intended changes and whose consumers were not updated. The change is documented and directionally correct, so it warrants a flag and a retro note rather than a block.
summary: REGRESSION validation of SD-LEO-INFRA-COORDINATOR-RECEIPTS-BROADCAST-CONSTRAINTS-001 against origin/main. 4929 consumer tests pass with zero failures; the single non-collecting suite is an untouched pre-existing parallel-run flake that passes 17/17 in isolation. resolveHoldProvenance revert confirmed byte-clean at +15/-0, comment only. Drain-set counts incremented by the arithmetically-forced delta and backed by a 4-row migration. Disjointness coverage strengthened, not loosened. Two findings raised: signal_receipt's classification flip shifting the pending and dead-letter lane gauges (MEDIUM), and universal WORK_ASSIGNMENT body mutation with vacuous existing-test coverage (LOW).
